title: Where do you live, what do you do
title_target: នៅឯណា ធ្វើការអ្វី — neuw 'ae-naa, thweu-kaa 'wey
goal: Say where you live and what you do, and master នៅ — one short word that does four different jobs and turns up in almost every Khmer sentence.
bekal: ask នៅឯណា? and answer it
say what you do with ខ្ញុំជា … and ខ្ញុំធ្វើការនៅ …
put the question word where the answer goes
talk about distance with ជិត and ឆ្ងាយ

dialogs.title: កិច្ចសន្ទនា — Tea on the veranda
dialogs.intro: Ani has come in. Sreymom pours the tea and starts asking questions — and, like almost every first-day conversation in Cambodia, her first two questions are where you live and what you do. Notice how many times the word នៅ appears and how many meanings it carries.

lines.text: [អានី|'aa-nii] [នៅ|neuw] [ឯណា|'ae-naa] [ចាស|chaah]?

grammars.title: ⚠️ នៅ — one short word, four jobs
body: នៅ (*neuw*) is the word you will hear most often in Cambodia after ខ្ញុំ. It never changes form; what changes is its place in the sentence, and that place decides its meaning.

head: Job
Example
Say it
Meaning
rows: ធ្វើការ**នៅ**សាលា
គាត់**នៅ**ក្នុងផ្ទះ

after: How do you tell "be somewhere" from "still"? Look at the word after it. **នៅ + place** = be/in/live. **នៅ + verb** = still. There are no exceptions to memorize at A1.

⚠️ Learners often look for a separate word for "at" or "in" and are surprised not to find one in some sentences: នៅផ្ទះ already means "at home" with nothing added. On the other hand, don't put នៅ in front of every place word — ខ្ញុំទៅផ្សារ ("I go to the market") does **not** use នៅ, because ទៅ already carries the direction.

grammars.title: Talking about work: ជា for your job, ធ្វើការ for your workplace
body: Khmer keeps apart two things: **who you are** and **where you work**. The first uses ជា ("to be"), the second uses ធ្វើការនៅ ("work at").

head: English
Khmer
Say it
rows: ខ្ញុំជាគ្រូ
ខ្ញុំធ្វើការនៅសាលា
អ្នកធ្វើការអ្វី?
ខ្ញុំមិនទាន់ធ្វើការទេ

after: ធ្វើ (*thweu*) on its own means "to do, to make", and ការ (*kaa*) means "work, affair" — from Sanskrit *kārya*, "deed". So ធ្វើការ is literally "do work". Once you notice ការ, you will find it everywhere: ការងារ (job), ការសិក្សា (education), ការរៀបការ (wedding).

grammars.title: The question word stands where the answer goes
body: This is one of Khmer's friendliest features. English moves the question word to the front of the sentence (*Where do you work?*). Khmer doesn't — the question word sits exactly in the seat the answer will take later: "you work where?".

head: Sentence
Say it
Translation
rows: អ្នកបង្រៀន**អ្វី**?
ខ្ញុំបង្រៀន**ភាសាខ្មែរ**

after: Notice that the question and its answer have **exactly the same** structure; only one word is swapped. If you can make the statement, you can already make the question.
⚠️ And remember the rule from unit 1: a sentence that already has a question word **does not use ទេ**. អ្នកនៅឯណាទេ? is a mistake. ទេ is only for yes/no questions.

blocks.title: Two Cambodian habits worth knowing
items: **Asking about someone's job is not rude.** In Cambodia, "what do you do?" and "where do you live?" are first-day questions. Nobody is offended, and refusing to answer actually feels odd.

**ជិត and ឆ្ងាយ are measured in time, not distance.** When a Cambodian says ជិត (near), they mean ten minutes by motorbike. ឆ្ងាយ means an hour or more. Asking "how many kilometers" is rarely useful; asking ប៉ុន្មាននាទី ("how many minutes") always is.
